status_alert: ACQUIRED / DELISTED. Nuveen, LLC (a TIAA company), via its subsidiary Pantheon LLC ('Bidco'), completed its £9.9bn (~$13.4-13.5bn) cash acquisition of Schroders plc by scheme of arrangement. Shareholders approved the deal with over 99% support in April 2026; all antitrust/regulatory conditions were satisfied or waived by late September 2026; the scheme received court sanction at a hearing on 29 September 2026; dealings in Schroders shares were suspended from 7.30am on 1 October 2026 and the LSE listing was cancelled by 8.00am on 2 October 2026. As of this analysis date (10 October 2026) Schroders plc is no longer an independently listed, investable security -- shareholders are entitled to receive up to 612p per share (590p cash plus up to 22p of permitted dividends). Schroders continues to operate as a distinct, Richard-Oldfield-led business within the combined Nuveen/Schroders group (reporting to Nuveen CEO Jose Minaya/leadership) for an expected 12-18 month integration period, creating a combined platform of roughly $2.5-2.6 trillion AUM. This report is retained for historical/research record; no forward DCF, dashboard or price-target work should be built on SDR.L as a going-concern independent equity.
overview: Schroders plc was a London-listed, FTSE 100, pure-play active asset manager and wealth manager with over two centuries of history, managing £823.7bn of AUM at FY2025 (rising to £867.8bn at H1 FY2026) across Public Markets (equities, fixed income, multi-asset, core solutions), Schroders Capital (private markets: private equity, private debt/credit alternatives, real estate, infrastructure) and Wealth Management (Cazenove Capital and Schroders Wealth Management serving high- and ultra-high-net-worth clients, family offices and charities). The Group operated globally (47% UK, 25% Asia Pacific, 16% EMEA, 12% Americas AUM) serving institutional (64%), intermediary (19%) and wealth (17%) clients, supplemented by joint ventures/associates in China (BOCOM), India (Axis Bank), Singapore (Nippon Life) and the UK (Phoenix Group). In February 2026 Schroders agreed to be acquired by Nuveen (TIAA's asset-management arm) for up to 612p/share (£9.9bn), and the deal completed with delisting from the LSE on 1-2 October 2026.

business_model.summary: Schroders earned revenue predominantly as ad-valorem management fees charged on AUM (a percentage of assets managed, varying by asset class and channel -- equities and private markets commanding materially higher margins than fixed income or core solutions), supplemented by smaller performance fees/carried interest, advisory and platform fees in Wealth Management, and returns on seed/co-investment capital deployed alongside clients in Schroders Capital. The large majority of revenue is recurring (AUM-linked, renews automatically absent redemptions) rather than transactional, though performance fees and private-markets carried interest introduce an episodic, market-cycle-dependent component. FY2025 adjusted net operating income was £2,589.8m (statutory net operating income £2,700.5m); FY2025 statutory revenue (restated, FY2025-comparable basis) was £3,250.7m with statutory operating profit of £673.9m (including a ~£113.3m one-off gain on the sale of Schroders' stake in the Schroders Personal Wealth (SPW) joint venture to Lloyds Banking Group -- strip this out for a cleaner run-rate). H1 FY2026 showed continued momentum: adjusted net operating income £1,419.2m (+17% YoY), adjusted operating profit £459.8m (+46% YoY), aided by a cost-to-income ratio improvement to 68% (FY2025: 71%) as the firm's three-year, £150m annualised cost-savings transformation programme reached >98% delivery 18 months in.

Wealth Management (Cazenove Capital, Schroders Wealth Management, Benchmark -- being sold)

Share of profit from joint ventures and associates (BOCOM China, Axis India, Nippon Life, Phoenix Group)

business_model.customer_type: Mixed institutional (pension funds, sovereign wealth funds, insurers -- 64% of AUM), intermediary/retail via platforms and fund distributors (19%), and private wealth -- high-net-worth, ultra-high-net-worth individuals, family offices and charities (17%) served through Cazenove Capital (UK) and Schroders Wealth Management (international).
business_model.geographic_mix: UK 47%, Asia Pacific 25%, EMEA (ex-UK) 16%, Americas 12% of AUM; sterling-denominated reporter with meaningful currency translation exposure given large non-GBP AUM and revenue base.

competitive_position.market_position: A top-five global asset management brand (per independent NMG Consulting research, held for seven years) and historically one of the top three European managers for fund performance (UBS research), but mid-sized relative to the scale giants (BlackRock, Vanguard, Amundi) in passive/index products, where Schroders does not materially compete. Positioned as a diversified, pure-play active manager spanning public and private markets plus a growing wealth franchise -- a differentiated combination versus narrower pure asset managers or pure private-markets specialists.

moat_factors.description: Top-5 global asset management brand (NMG Consulting); 220+ year operating history; institutional relationships spanning 25+ years with some clients, and private wealth relationships spanning multiple generations (one family served 75+ years), supporting high retention and referral-driven growth.

70-73% of client AUM outperformed benchmarks over one/three/five years in FY2025, among the top three European managers for listed-fund performance per UBS research over six years -- performance quality that underpins fee retention and new mandate wins (e.g., £3.3bn PGGM, £4.0bn St. James's Place mandates in 2025).

moat_factors.factor: Breadth across public and private markets plus wealth
moat_factors.description: Few competitors of similar scale offer the full combination of listed equities/fixed income, private markets (Schroders Capital) and HNW/UHNW wealth management under one roof, enabling cross-referral and integrated public-private solutions -- though this breadth is itself expensive to maintain and dilutes focus versus specialists.

Partnerships with BOCOM (China), Axis Bank (India), Nippon Life (Singapore) and Phoenix Group (UK) provide access and distribution reach in markets where organic build-out would be slow or capital-intensive, though JV profit contribution is modest and was reduced further by the FY2025 SPW stake disposal.

Institutional mandates and HNW wealth relationships carry moderate switching costs (due diligence cycles, advisory relationships), but retail/intermediary fund flows are highly mobile and price-sensitive, limiting pricing power versus passive alternatives.

weaknesses: Sub-scale versus the largest global passive/index managers (BlackRock, Vanguard) and even some active peers, limiting unit-cost advantages in commoditising segments
Years of net outflows/subdued organic growth in core Public Markets prior to the 2025-2027 transformation programme, with persistent fee-margin pressure industry-wide
Complexity from operating across many legal entities, markets and a wealth-management business (Benchmark) that was ultimately deemed non-core and sold
Dependence on favorable capital markets for AUM growth, performance fees and seed/co-investment returns -- a cyclical, market-beta-exposed business model despite active management positioning

Smaller scale than Nuveen/TIAA's combined post-acquisition platform was itself evidence that independent scale was becoming a constraint, prompting the board to accept a sale rather than pursue standalone transformation to its conclusion

growth_drivers: COMPLETED: Combination with Nuveen (TIAA) -- closed 1-2 October 2026, creating a ~$2.5-2.6 trillion AUM public-to-private global platform; no longer a forward driver for SDR.L equity but the defining event of the research period

Three-year transformation programme (launched March 2025): £150m annualised net cost savings target, >98% delivered by H1 FY2026, driving cost-to-income ratio to 68% (ahead of the <70% target originally set for end-2027)

Scaling Schroders Capital (private markets): committed to £20bn cumulative net new business 2025-2027; £500m of Group seed/co-investment capital committed to support fund launches (e.g., Greencoat Global Fund, BlueOrchard Climate Action Mobilisation Fund)

Active ETF expansion: European active ETF range reached $3.5bn AUM within 12 months of launch, achieving a top-10 UCITS active ETF position; existing capabilities in the US and Australia being extended

Portfolio simplification and capital redeployment: exits from Brazil, Indonesia, South Korea restructuring, Munich real estate, Australian private credit and the agreed sale of Benchmark (UK advice platform) to concentrate capital and management attention on higher-return segments

Wealth Management refocus: regained full ownership of Cazenove Capital (in exchange for the Schroders Personal Wealth stake, given to Lloyds Banking Group) to build a more focused UK/international HNW and UHNW wealth franchise

New distribution partnerships: £3.3bn PGGM sustainable equity mandate, £4.0bn St. James's Place mandate, Mercer UK DC/LTAF mandate, and a February 2026 strategic partnership with Apollo on public-private investment solutions

business.description: Structural industry-wide shift toward passive and lower-cost strategies continues to pressure active management fee margins, particularly in core equities and fixed income; management explicitly flagged this within 'business model disruption' as a principal risk.

Client retention and new mandate wins depend on sustaining above-benchmark performance (70-73% of AUM outperformed in FY2025); a performance downturn could trigger redemptions, as competitors aggressively target underperforming strategies.

business.risk: Net flow volatility / institutional concentration risk
business.description: H1 FY2026 showed a £6.6bn low-margin institutional mandate redemption and historically volatile net new business; large single mandates (wins or losses) can swing headline flow figures materially.

business.risk: Integration and cultural risk post-Nuveen acquisition
business.description: Now the dominant forward-looking risk: successful integration into Nuveen/TIAA over the next 12-18 months, retention of key investment talent and client relationships through an ownership change, and realization of promised synergies from the ~$2.5tn combined platform.

financial.description: Sterling reporting against a large non-GBP AUM and revenue base (53% of AUM outside the UK) creates translation volatility; FX reduced AUM by £18.4bn in FY2025 alone.

financial.risk: Seed and co-investment capital market risk
financial.description: Up to £500m of Group balance-sheet capital committed to Schroders Capital seed/co-investments carries direct market and credit risk exposure, albeit partially hedged.

regulatory.description: Operating across many jurisdictions exposes the firm to an extensive, evolving compliance burden, including UK PRA/FCA requirements, the EU's Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA), Basel 3.1-aligned counterparty standards, and financial-crime/AML regimes.

The Nuveen acquisition's completion required antitrust and regulatory clearances across multiple jurisdictions; all were satisfied or waived by late September 2026 and the scheme received UK court sanction on 29 September 2026, removing this risk.

macro.description: AUM, and therefore fee revenue, performance fees and adjusted operating profit, are directly linked to global equity, fixed income and private-market valuations; a sustained market downturn or volatility spike would reduce average AUM and revenue even absent net outflows.

macro.risk: Interest rate and credit cycle sensitivity
macro.description: Fixed income and credit-oriented strategies, plus private debt/credit alternatives within Schroders Capital, are sensitive to rate and spread movements; elevated long-term rates and fiscal-sustainability concerns were flagged by management as an emerging macro theme.

Protectionism, tariffs, sanctions regimes and conflict risk can disrupt cross-border client servicing, specific country exposures (e.g., prior exits from Brazil, Indonesia, South Korea restructuring) and joint-venture operations in China and India.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global active asset management faces structural fee pressure from passive/index products, but demand for active management is being supported by elevated market concentration risk (index-level concentration in mega-cap technology names), rising investor appetite for private markets/alternatives, and demographic/wealth-transfer tailwinds in HNW/UHNW wealth management. M&A consolidation across the sector (of which the Nuveen/Schroders deal is itself a leading 2026 example) reflects industry-wide recognition that scale, cost discipline and public-private breadth are increasingly necessary for profitable growth.
macro_factors.cyclicality: High -- AUM-linked fee revenue, performance fees and seed/co-investment returns are all directly geared to financial market levels and volatility; net flows are also pro-cyclical, tending to deteriorate in risk-off periods even before performance effects.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate -- affects fixed income/credit strategy AUM and valuations, private debt economics within Schroders Capital, and discount rates applied to insurance-linked and other liability-style assets managed on clients' behalf; limited direct balance-sheet leverage (Schroders itself carried minimal net debt, ~£256m gross debt against £3.6-4.6bn cash).
key_input_costs: Compensation and variable bonus costs (the largest single cost line, ~65% of adjusted operating expenses)
Technology, outsourcing and third-party/cloud service costs (expanding via the UST partnership)
Real estate/office costs (including a one-off £20m remedial building-works charge in FY2025)

recent_developments.event: Nuveen's £9.9bn (~$13.4bn) acquisition of Schroders completed; trading in Schroders shares suspended from 7.30am on 1 October 2026 and the LSE listing cancelled by 8.00am on 2 October 2026. Schroders becomes a subsidiary of Nuveen/TIAA, continuing to operate as a distinct business under CEO Richard Oldfield for an expected 12-18 month integration period.
UK court sanction hearing approved the scheme of arrangement, clearing the final procedural step before completion.
Schroders and Nuveen confirmed all antitrust and regulatory conditions for the acquisition had been satisfied or waived.

H1 FY2026 results: record AUM of £867.8bn; adjusted net operating income +17% to £1,419.2m; adjusted operating profit +46% to £459.8m; statutory profit before tax +102% to £396.8m; interim dividend raised to 7.0p (H1 2025: 6.5p); cost-to-income ratio improved to 68%, hitting the <70% target 18 months into the three-year transformation programme; agreed sale of Benchmark (UK financial advice business) announced; completed exits from Brazil and Indonesia.
Schroders shareholders approved the Nuveen acquisition with over 99% of votes in favour at a general meeting.

Schroders and Nuveen (TIAA) announced the recommended £9.9bn cash acquisition at up to 612p/share (590p cash + up to 22p permitted dividends), a ~29-34% premium to the undisturbed share price; holders of ~42% of shares gave irrevocable undertakings to support the deal.

FY2025 annual results: adjusted operating profit £756.6m (+25% YoY, on a FY2025 pre-SPW-gain adjusted basis per the KPI table) / statutory operating profit of £673.9m including a ~£113.3m one-off gain on the sale of the Schroders Personal Wealth (SPW) JV stake to Lloyds Banking Group; FY2024 operating profit restated to £528.8m on a comparable basis; AUM reached a then-record £823.7bn; full-year dividend held flat at 21.5p; announced a strategic partnership with Apollo on public-private investment solutions.

guidance.as_of: H1 FY2026 Results (30 July 2026) -- last results published as an independently listed company before the Nuveen acquisition completed
guidance.fiscal_year: FY2026 (final full year as an independent listed entity; company now a Nuveen subsidiary)

items.period: Original target: end of 2027 (three-year transformation programme from March 2025)
items.notes: Already achieved (68% at H1 FY2026, down from 71% at FY2025) roughly 18 months into the three-year programme, well ahead of the original end-2027 target.
Over 98% delivered by H1 FY2026, with 'a clear line of sight to the remaining efficiencies' expected to complete in H2 2026.
£4.6bn delivered in FY2025 against the three-year £20bn target; management acknowledged the need not to be complacent given subdued global private-markets fundraising.

items.metric: Wealth Management net new business rate
items.vs_prior: below target in FY2025 (2.7% actual) but improving -- Cazenove Capital NNB rate reached 5% at H1 FY2026
items.notes: UK private client book alone ran above target (5.2% in FY2025); overall rate dragged down by charities outflows and muted Benchmark flows (Benchmark since agreed for sale).
Net operating revenue already increasing (+5% FY2025, +24% H1 FY2026) rather than merely stabilising, aided by favourable markets and channel/regional mix.

guidance.management_commentary: At H1 FY2026, Group CEO Richard Oldfield highlighted 'record AUM of £867.8 billion, alongside double-digit revenue growth' and 'positive client sentiment towards our proposed combination with Nuveen,' while flagging that 'markets will remain unpredictable.' This was the Group's last standalone guidance update before the Nuveen acquisition completed on 1-2 October 2026; no further independent forward guidance from Schroders plc as a listed entity should be expected.

bull_case: Deal is done: shareholders who held through completion received up to 612p/share in cash (590p cash plus up to 22p permitted dividends), a 29-34% premium to the undisturbed 456p share price -- for prior holders, the thesis has already been realized via the takeover rather than ongoing equity upside

Transformation programme delivered ahead of schedule: >98% of the £150m annualised cost-savings target achieved roughly 18 months into a three-year plan, with cost-to-income ratio already below the original end-2027 target of 70%

Strong underlying momentum into the deal close: H1 FY2026 adjusted operating profit up 46% YoY, record AUM of £867.8bn, and improving net new business trends (Cazenove Capital NNB rate at 5%, Schroders Capital's best quarterly fundraising in three years)

Combined Nuveen/Schroders platform (~$2.5-2.6tn AUM) creates one of the world's largest global active asset managers with a genuinely scaled public-to-private investment capability, a complementarity the companies argue should support growth prospects for the combined business and its stakeholders (including any continuing Schroders family/legacy shareholders or TIAA policyholders) longer term

Clean, largely de-risked completion: all antitrust/regulatory approvals secured, court sanction obtained, and integration structured to preserve Schroders' operating identity and CEO for 12-18 months, reducing near-term execution risk relative to a typical cross-border M&A integration
bear_case: Not investable going forward: Schroders plc delisted from the LSE on 1-2 October 2026 and no longer trades as an independent public equity -- there is no forward total-return thesis in SDR.L shares beyond the already-paid takeover consideration

Critics (e.g., Panmure Liberum) argued the 612p/590p offer price was too low relative to Schroders' standalone turnaround trajectory, implying existing shareholders may have sold out cheaply just as the transformation programme's cost savings and operating leverage were beginning to show through in H1 FY2026's 46% profit growth

Pre-deal fundamentals carried real risk even absent the acquisition: persistent fee compression from passive competition, historically volatile net flows (including a sizeable £6.6bn low-margin institutional redemption in H1 FY2026), and continued underperformance versus the 5-7% Wealth Management NNB target

Integration risk now sits with Nuveen/TIAA, not with independent Schroders shareholders: successful realization of the combined ~$2.5tn platform's promised synergies, talent retention through an ownership change, and cultural integration between a US insurance-affiliated manager and a historic UK institution are unresolved execution risks for the surviving entity

One-off items complicate any attempt to extrapolate pre-deal Schroders financials: FY2025's £673.9m statutory operating profit included a ~£113.3m one-off gain on the SPW stake sale, and FY2024 operating profit was itself restated (£640.5m originally reported vs. £528.8m restated), underscoring that reported profit trends required careful normalization even before the sale process began

sector_classification.notes: Pure-play active asset manager plus a growing private wealth management division; not a bank, insurer or broker-dealer. As of 2 October 2026 the company is a wholly owned subsidiary of Nuveen, LLC (a TIAA company) and is no longer separately listed; classify any remaining historical data as a delisted/acquired security, not a going concern for screening or DCF purposes.
